84647.e: A screenshot is a still picture. That is why it is saved as an image file.
84647.m: A screenshot is saved as a picture.

84648.q: What is it called when you record the screen like a film?
84648.e: With a screen recording, everything that happens on the screen is saved as a video. A screenshot, on the other hand, only shows one moment.
84648.m: A screen recording saves the screen as a video.

84649.e: A video shows pictures that move. Usually you hear sound with it too.
84649.m: A video shows moving pictures, often with sound.

84650.q: What is a video actually made of?
84650.e: A video shows lots of pictures one after another very quickly. Our eyes see a smooth movement.
84650.m: A video is made of lots of single pictures shown quickly.

84651.q: Which symbol does the button for playing a video usually have?
84651.e: The triangle pointing to the right means play.

84652.q: What do two vertical lines on a video button mean?
84652.e: With the pause button the video stops. If you press it again, it carries on from the same place.

84653.q: What does a square on a video button usually mean?
84653.e: The square ends playback. After that the video often starts again from the beginning.
84653.m: A square on a button means stop.

84654.q: What is it called when you cut out parts of a video and put them together again?
84654.e: In video editing you remove boring bits and arrange the scenes. There are special programs and apps for this.
84654.m: In video editing a video is shortened and put together.

84655.q: How do you hold your phone so that a video is wide like on a television?
84655.e: A television is wider than it is tall. If you hold your phone sideways, the video has the same wide shape.
84655.m: For a wide video you hold your phone sideways.

84656.q: Roughly how many pictures per second does a video show?
84656.e: Many videos show 25 or 30 pictures every second. That is so fast that the movement looks smooth.
84656.m: A video shows about 25 to 30 pictures every second.

84657.q: What is the text at the bottom of a video that shows what is being said called?
84657.e: Subtitles write what is said as text on the screen. They help, for example, people who cannot hear well.
84657.m: Subtitles show what is said as text.

84658.q: What do you record sounds and voices with?
84658.e: A microphone turns sound into electrical signals. The device can then save them.
84658.m: You record sounds with a microphone.

84659.q: What do you use to play back a sound recording out loud in the room?
84659.e: A loudspeaker turns saved sounds back into sound you can hear. With headphones you listen on your own.

a: A programme to listen to on the internet
A photo album on the internet
84660.e: You can listen to a podcast on the internet whenever you like. There are often lots of episodes on one topic.
84660.m: A podcast is a listening programme from the internet.

84661.q: What can disturb a sound recording outdoors especially badly?
84661.e: Wind blows into the microphone and makes loud rushing noises. A windshield made of foam or fur helps against this.
84661.m: Wind can make a sound recording outdoors rush loudly.

84662.q: Where does a voice recording work best?
84662.e: In a quiet room there are no disturbing noises. That way the voice sounds clear.
84662.m: For good sound recordings you look for a quiet place.

84663.q: What does the jagged line that appears on the screen while recording show?
84663.e: The jagged line shows the sound wave. Big peaks mean loud sounds, small peaks quiet sounds.
84663.m: Big peaks in the sound wave mean loud sounds.

84664.q: What is a short sound recording that you send in a chat called?
84664.e: With a voice message you speak into the phone instead of writing. The other person listens to it later.
84664.m: A voice message is a spoken message in a chat.

84665.q: Which is a well-known format for sound files?
84665.e: MP3 is a very common format for music and speech. JPG, PNG and GIF are formats for pictures.
84665.m: MP3 is a well-known format for sound files.

84666.q: Why should you not speak too far away from the microphone when recording?
a: So the file is more colourful
84666.e: If you are too far away, the voice sounds quiet and other noises get louder. Close to the microphone you can be understood better.
84666.m: If you speak close to the microphone, you can be heard more clearly.

84667.e: Emojis are small pictures such as faces, animals or food. You put them in messages.
84667.m: Emojis are small pictures in messages.

84668.q: Which language does the word “emoji” come from?
84668.e: Emoji is Japanese: “e” means picture and “moji” means written character. The first emojis were on Japanese mobile phones.
84668.m: The word emoji comes from Japan.

84669.q: What do people often use emojis for in messages?
84669.e: A laughing or sad face shows how you feel. In written messages this helps you to be understood correctly.
84669.m: With emojis you can show feelings in messages.

84670.q: What does a thumbs-up emoji usually mean?
84670.e: The raised thumb is a sign of agreement. People often use it as a short “OK”.

84671.e: World Emoji Day is celebrated every year on 17 July. The date comes from the calendar emoji, which often shows 17 July.
84671.m: World Emoji Day is on 17 July.

84672.q: What does the sequence of characters :-) mean in a message?
84672.e: If you tilt your head to the side, you see eyes, a nose and a smiling mouth. Faces made of characters like this existed even before emojis.
84672.m: You can write a smiling face with punctuation marks.

84673.q: Does an emoji look exactly the same on every phone?
a: No, it looks a little different depending on the device
No, it always becomes black and white
Yes, but only in the evening
84673.e: Each company draws its own emojis. The meaning is the same, but colours and shapes can be different.
84673.m: An emoji can look different on different devices.

84674.q: What does an emoji with a tear and a sad mouth show?
84674.e: A tear and a mouth curved downwards stand for sadness. You use it to show that something is getting you down.

84675.q: What does a photo filter in an app do?
84675.e: A filter changes, for example, colours, brightness or contrast with one click. The photo then looks different.
84675.m: A photo filter changes how a photo looks with one click.

84676.q: What does a black-and-white filter do?
84676.e: With a black-and-white filter only black, white and shades of grey are left. The photo then looks like an old picture.
84676.m: A black-and-white filter shows a photo only in shades of grey.

84677.q: Which filter makes a photo look brownish and old?
84677.e: Sepia is a brownish colour. Many very old photos have this colour.
84677.m: A sepia filter gives photos an old, brown tone.

84678.q: What do some funny filters put on a face in the camera?
84678.e: Filters like these recognise the face and put pictures over it. They move along when you move your head.
84678.m: Funny filters put pictures like animal ears on a face.

84679.q: A filter makes faces smoother and prettier. What does that mean for photos on the internet?
a: People look different from real life
There are no filters on the internet
84679.e: Many photos on the internet have been made prettier with filters. Real faces have wrinkles, spots and bumps.
84679.m: Photos with filters often show people differently from how they really look.

84680.q: Which filter makes a picture soft and blurry?
84680.e: The blur filter smudges fine details. You can use it, for example, to make a background blurry.
84680.m: With the blur filter a picture becomes blurry.

84681.q: What gets stronger when you increase the contrast of a photo?
a: The difference between light and dark
84681.e: With more contrast, light areas get lighter and dark areas darker. The picture looks bolder.
84681.m: More contrast makes light and dark more different.

84682.q: A filter gives a photo a slightly bluish colour. How does the photo usually feel then?
84682.e: We link blue with cold, water and ice. Red and orange shades, on the other hand, feel warm.
84682.m: Blue shades make a photo feel cool.

a: A film made of lots of single photos
84683.e: You photograph a figure, move it a little and photograph it again. If you play the photos quickly, it seems to move.
84683.m: A stop-motion film is made of lots of single photos.

84684.q: In stop motion, what do you do between two photos?
a: You move the figure a tiny bit
84684.e: Each photo shows the figure only a little bit differently. That creates movement when you play it back.
84684.m: In stop motion you move the figure only a tiny bit between photos.

84685.q: What material are stop-motion figures often made of?
84685.e: Modelling clay is easy to shape and stays in any position. That is why it is very popular for animated films.
84685.m: Clay figures are very popular in stop-motion films.

84686.q: What is the name of the little clay penguin from a well-known Swiss animated series?
84686.e: Pingu is a stop-motion series from Switzerland that started in 1990. The penguin speaks his own made-up language.
84686.m: Pingu is a stop-motion penguin from Switzerland.

84687.q: Why do you put the camera on a tripod for stop motion?
84687.e: If the camera moves between the photos, the whole film wobbles. A tripod keeps it in the same place all the time.
84687.m: A tripod keeps the camera still for stop motion.

84688.q: What happens if you move the figure much too far between two photos?
84688.e: You can clearly see big jumps between the pictures. Small steps give a smooth movement.
84688.m: Small steps make a stop-motion movement smooth.

84689.q: Lina needs 10 photos for one second of stop-motion film. How many photos does she need for 3 seconds?
84689.e: She needs 10 photos for each second. 3 times 10 makes 30 photos.
84689.m: For longer stop-motion films you need a great many photos.

84690.q: Which sheep is a famous star of clay animation films?
84690.e: Shaun the Sheep is a stop-motion character from England. The films manage almost without words.
84690.m: Shaun the Sheep is a well-known stop-motion character.

84691.q: Which device is enough to make a simple stop-motion film?
84691.e: With a stop-motion app, the tablet takes the pictures and puts them together into a film straight away. You can do this at school too.
84691.m: You can make stop-motion films with a tablet and an app.

84692.q: What is a photo album for?
a: To collect and look at photos
84692.e: In a photo album photos are kept in order. That way you can remember experiences later.
84692.m: In a photo album you collect photos to remember things.

84693.q: Where do you find a digital photo album?
84693.e: A digital album is a folder or collection in a photo app. The photos are saved as files.
84693.m: Digital photo albums are saved on a phone or computer.

84694.q: What is a sensible way to sort photos in an album?
84694.e: If you sort by date, you easily find holidays or birthdays again. Many apps sort photos like this automatically.
84694.m: Photos are often sorted by date.

84695.q: What is a printed book with your own photos called?
84695.e: You design a photo book on the computer and then have it printed. The photos are printed on the pages of the book.
84695.m: A photo book is a printed book with your own photos.

84696.q: Why do you make a backup copy of important photos?
a: So they do not get lost
84696.e: A phone can break or get lost. With a copy in another place, the photos are kept safe.
84696.m: A backup copy protects photos from being lost.

a: Photos are shown one after another
84697.e: In a slideshow the photos in an album appear automatically one after the other. Often music plays as well.
84697.m: In a slideshow photos are shown one after another.

84698.q: What do people often write next to a photo in an album?
a: Where and when it was taken
84698.e: A short caption helps you remember later. Place and date are especially useful.
84698.m: A caption with place and date helps you remember.

84699.q: What is the best thing to do with blurry or duplicate photos?
84699.e: Unnecessary photos take up storage space and make the album messy. That is why you sort them out.
84699.m: Deleting unnecessary photos gives you a tidier album.

84700.q: What is the memory card in a digital camera for?
84700.e: The memory card is a small data store. The photos and videos are saved on it.
84700.m: Photos and videos are stored on the memory card.

a: A card for making phone calls
84701.e: A microSD card is hardly bigger than a fingernail. Phones or small cameras store photos and videos on it.
84701.m: A microSD card is a very small memory card.

84702.q: Which unit is often used to give the storage space of a memory card?
84702.e: A gigabyte is a unit for amounts of data, shortened to GB. The more gigabytes, the more fits on it.
84702.m: Storage space is measured in gigabytes, for example.

84703.q: What happens when a camera's memory card is full?
a: You cannot save any new photos
84703.e: If there is no space left, the camera cannot store new pictures. You have to delete photos or put in a new card.
84703.m: When the memory card is full, no new photos fit on it.

84704.q: Which memory card holds more photos?
84704.e: 64 GB is the biggest storage space in this choice. That is why the most photos fit on it.
84704.m: The more gigabytes a card has, the more photos fit on it.

84705.q: Which device do you use to read a memory card on a computer?
84705.e: A card reader has a slot for the card. With it the computer can open the photos on the card.
84705.m: With a card reader you get photos from the memory card onto the computer.

84706.q: What usually takes up more space on a memory card?
84706.e: A video is made of a great many pictures plus sound. That is why it is much bigger than a single photo.
84706.m: Videos need much more storage space than photos.

84707.q: When should you not take a memory card out of the camera?
84707.e: If you take the card out while it is saving, photos can be damaged. You wait until the camera has finished.
84707.m: While saving, the memory card stays in the camera.

84708.q: What are the very fine little hairs on a root called?
84708.e: The fine root hairs sit near the tip of the root. With them the plant takes up especially large amounts of water.
84708.m: Root hairs help the plant drink water.

84709.q: What is the long main root of the dandelion, which grows straight down, called?
84709.e: The dandelion has a thick taproot. It grows deep and straight down into the ground.

84710.q: Which way does a root normally grow?
84710.e: Roots grow downwards in the direction of gravity. That way they find water in the soil.

84711.q: What does ivy use to climb up walls and trees?
84711.e: Ivy grows small clinging roots on its stem. It uses them to hold on tightly to walls.

84712.q: Why are plants important on a steep slope?
a: Their roots hold the soil in place
84712.e: The roots of many plants hold the soil together. So the earth is not washed away so easily when it rains.
84712.m: Roots hold the soil on a slope in place.

84713.q: Which part of the plant carries the leaves and flowers?
84713.e: The stem grows up out of the ground. The leaves and flowers sit on it.
84713.m: The stem carries the leaves and flowers.

84714.q: What does the stem carry up from the root?
84714.e: There are fine tubes in the stem. Water flows through them from the root up into the leaves.

84715.q: What is the hollow stem of cereals and grasses called?
84715.e: Grasses and cereals such as wheat have a thin, hollow stem. It is called a culm.

84716.e: Plants need light to live. That is why their stems grow towards the light.

84717.q: A white flower is standing in water with blue food colouring. What happens after a while?
84717.e: The stem sucks the coloured water up to the flower. That is why the white petals turn bluish.
84717.m: The stem carries water up to the flower.

84718.q: Which part of the plant do you eat with asparagus?
84718.e: With asparagus you eat the young shoots. They are cut before they get big.
84718.m: With asparagus you eat young stems.

84719.e: Leaves contain a green pigment called chlorophyll. With it, the leaf captures sunlight.

84720.q: Which tree has leaves that look like needles?
84720.e: The fir is a conifer. Its needles are narrow, hard leaves.

84721.q: Which part of the plant attracts insects with colours and scent?
84721.e: Flowers are often colourful and scented. That is how bees and other insects find their way to them.

84723.q: Which way do young sunflowers turn their heads during the day?
84723.e: Young sunflowers follow the sun from east to west. Fully grown sunflowers usually stay facing east.
84723.m: Young sunflowers look towards the sun.

84725.q: When does the evening primrose open its yellow flowers?
84725.e: The evening primrose opens its flowers at dusk. Then moths visit them.
84725.m: The evening primrose opens in the evening.

84726.q: The daisy looks like one flower. What is it really?
84726.e: The head of the daisy is made of lots and lots of tiny flowers. The yellow ones sit in the middle, the white ones around the edge.
84726.m: A daisy is made of lots of small flowers.

84727.q: What grows from a cherry blossom later on?
84727.e: A cherry develops from the pollinated cherry blossom. The seed is inside the stone.
84727.m: A cherry blossom becomes a cherry.

84728.q: What are the coloured parts of a flower called?
84728.e: The colourful parts of the flower are called petals. They are often soft and delicate.

84729.q: What happens to the petals after the flower has been pollinated?
84729.e: After pollination the plant no longer needs the petals. They wilt while the fruit starts to grow.

84730.q: How many petals does a yellow rapeseed flower have?
84730.e: Rapeseed belongs to the cabbage family, whose flowers form a cross. Its four petals are arranged like a cross.
84730.m: The rapeseed flower has four petals.

84731.q: How many petals does an apple blossom have?
84731.e: The apple blossom has five white to pink petals. That is typical of the rose family.

84732.q: Which oil can be made from petals?
84732.e: To make rose oil you need lots and lots of scented rose petals. Olive oil and sunflower oil come from fruits and seeds.

84733.q: Which field flower has bright red, thin petals?
84733.e: The common poppy grows at the edge of fields. Its red petals are as thin as tissue paper.

84734.q: What colour are the petals of the cornflower?
84734.e: The cornflower likes to grow in fields of grain. Its flowers are a strong, bright blue.

84735.q: What do you call a young flower that is still closed?
84735.e: Before a flower opens, it is folded up into a bud. Inside, it is well protected.
84735.m: A closed flower is called a bud.

84736.q: When do the buds that open on trees in spring form?
84736.e: Trees form their buds as early as summer and autumn. In spring they just have to open.
84736.m: Tree buds form in the year before.

84737.q: What wraps and protects buds in winter?
84737.e: Hard bud scales wrap the bud like a coat. So it does not dry out in winter.

84738.q: What comes out of a leaf bud?
84738.e: Small folded leaves lie inside a leaf bud. In spring they unfold.
84738.m: Leaves grow out of a leaf bud.

84739.q: Which tree has fat, sticky buds?
84739.e: The buds of the horse chestnut are fat and shiny and sticky. The sticky coating protects them from wet and from animals.
84739.m: The horse chestnut has sticky buds.

84740.q: What is the bud right at the tip of a twig called?
84740.e: The terminal bud sits at the tip of the twig. In spring the twig grows on from it.
84740.m: The terminal bud sits at the tip of the twig.

84741.e: Cloves are the dried flower buds of a tropical tree. They look like little nails.

84742.q: Which part of the plant do you mainly eat with broccoli?
84742.e: The green florets of broccoli are lots of small flower buds. If you leave them, they open into yellow flowers.
84742.m: With broccoli you eat flower buds.

84743.q: Which small green pickled balls are really flower buds?
84743.e: Capers are the flower buds of the caper bush. They are pickled in salt or vinegar.

84744.q: Why do many plants have thorns or prickles?
84744.e: Sharp thorns and prickles hurt. So the plants are eaten by animals less often.

84745.q: The rose actually has no thorns. What does it have instead?
84745.e: The sharp parts of the rose are prickles. They only sit on the outside of the bark.

84746.q: Which is easy to break off a twig: prickles or thorns?
84746.e: Prickles only grow out of the outer skin. Thorns, on the other hand, are firmly joined to the wood.
84746.m: Prickles break off more easily than thorns.

84747.q: What are the spines of a cactus really?
84747.e: The spines of cacti developed from leaves. They have become narrow and hard.

84748.q: Which shrub with white flowers has the word thorn in its name?
84748.e: The hawthorn has white flowers and sharp thorns. It often grows in hedges.

84749.q: What does the blackberry have on its shoots that pricks you when you pick the berries?
84749.e: Blackberry shoots are covered in lots of prickles. So you have to be careful when picking.

84750.q: Which berry bush has the word “prickle” in its German name?
84750.e: The gooseberry has sharp prickles on its branches. That is why its German name means “prickle berry”.

84751.q: What does a plant need tendrils for?
84751.e: Tendrils wrap around supports. That way the plant can climb upwards.

84752.q: Which garden plant climbs with tendrils?
84752.e: The pea has fine tendrils. With them it holds on to sticks or nets.

84753.q: On which plant with tendrils do grapes grow?
84753.e: The grapevine holds on to wires with its tendrils. Grapes grow on it.

84754.q: What does a tendril do when it touches a stick?
84754.e: Tendrils can feel touch. Then they grow more on one side and wrap around the support.

84755.e: Many tendrils curl up into spirals. It looks like a little spring.
84755.m: Tendrils are often twisted like a spiral.

84756.e: The cucumber grows long tendrils. With them it climbs up trellises.

84757.q: What did the tendrils of the pea develop from?
84757.e: In the pea, parts of the leaves have turned into tendrils. They are called leaf tendrils.

84758.q: What does a climbing plant with tendrils need in the garden to grow well?
a: A support such as a trellis
84758.e: Plants with tendrils need something to hold on to. A trellis, a net or sticks are ideal.
84758.m: Plants with tendrils need a support.

84759.q: Which flower grows from a bulb?
84759.e: Tulips grow from flower bulbs. The sunflower, on the other hand, grows from a seed.
84759.m: The tulip grows from a bulb.

84760.q: What does a flower bulb store?
84760.e: Food is stored in the bulb. With it, the plant can sprout quickly in spring.
84760.m: The bulb is a food store.

84761.q: What are the layers of an onion made of?
84761.e: The layers of an onion are thickened leaves. They sit on a short stem.

84762.q: Which yellow spring flower grows from a bulb and is also called a narcissus?
84762.e: The daffodil is a narcissus. It grows from a bulb and flowers around Easter.
84762.m: The daffodil grows from a bulb.

84763.q: What often happens when you cut an onion?
84763.e: When you cut it, a substance forms that rises into the air. It irritates your eyes, so they water.
84763.m: Cutting onions makes your eyes water.

84764.q: How do you put a flower bulb into the ground?
84764.e: The shoot grows out of the tip, and the roots form at the bottom. So the tip goes upwards.
84764.m: The tip of the bulb points upwards.

84765.q: Which flavouring is a bulb made of several small cloves?
84765.e: A head of garlic is made of several small cloves. In botany it is a bulb.

84766.q: Where do potatoes grow on the potato plant?
84766.e: Potatoes grow on underground shoots. That is why you have to dig them up.

84767.q: What are the “eyes” of a potato?
84767.e: The eyes are buds on the tuber. New shoots grow out of them.
84767.m: The eyes of a potato are buds.

84768.q: What colour do potatoes turn in the light, so that you should not eat those parts?
84768.e: In the light, potatoes turn green and make a poisonous substance. Cut green parts away generously.
84768.m: Don’t eat the green parts of potatoes.

84769.q: Which parts of the potato plant do people eat?
84769.e: People only eat the tubers. The green berries and the leaves of the plant are poisonous.
84769.m: With the potato, you only eat the tubers.

84770.q: Which vegetable is a fat swelling that grows above the ground?
84770.e: With kohlrabi the stem swells just above the ground. This forms a round bulb-like tuber.

84771.q: What does the potato mainly store in its tuber?
84771.e: The potato stores lots of starch. Starch is a nutrient that fills us up.

84772.q: What do you put in the ground in spring to get new potatoes?
84772.e: You plant seed potatoes in the ground. New plants with lots of tubers grow out of their eyes.

84773.q: What carries the pollen of grasses and hazel bushes?
84773.e: Grasses and hazel have very light pollen. The wind blows it to other plants.
84773.m: With grasses, the wind carries the pollen.

84774.q: Which allergy can pollen cause in some people?
84774.e: With hay fever the body reacts to pollen. Your nose runs and your eyes itch.

84775.q: What do bees carry in little lumps on their back legs?
84775.e: Bees comb pollen together and stick it to their back legs. These lumps are called pollen loads.

84776.q: What do bees need the pollen they collect for?
84776.e: Pollen contains a lot of protein. Bees feed their larvae with it.
84776.m: Pollen is bee food for the larvae.

84777.q: Which shrub in Switzerland often releases a lot of pollen as early as February?
84777.e: The hazel flowers very early in the year. Its yellow catkins release pollen even in winter.

84778.q: Which small bird drinks nectar and can hover in the air?
84778.e: The hummingbird beats its wings very fast. So it hovers in front of the flower and drinks nectar.

84779.q: What does a butterfly drink nectar with?
84779.e: Butterflies have a long sucking tube called a proboscis. When they don’t need it, they roll it up.

84780.q: Why do flowers offer nectar to insects?
a: So that the insects fall asleep
So that the flower gets heavier
84780.e: Sweet nectar attracts insects. While they drink, they carry pollen on.
84780.m: Nectar is a reward for insects.

84781.q: Where is the nectar usually found in a flower?
84781.e: The nectar usually lies at the bottom of the flower. On the way there, the insect brushes against pollen.
84781.m: Nectar lies deep in the flower.

84782.q: What do bees let evaporate from nectar so that it turns into honey?
84782.e: Nectar is very watery. The bees let most of the water evaporate until thick honey forms.

84783.q: What usually comes out first when a seed sprouts?
84783.e: When a seed sprouts, the little root pushes out first. That way the seedling can soon take up water.
84783.m: When a seed sprouts, the root comes first.

84784.q: What happens to the roots of a pot plant that is always standing in water?
a: They grow out of the pot into the air
They become as hard as wood
84784.e: Roots need air too. If they are always standing in water, they get too little air and start to rot.
84784.m: Too much water makes roots rot.

84785.q: Which trees stand in the water on long stilt roots along tropical coasts?
84785.e: Mangroves grow in salty water on warm coasts. Their stilt roots hold them firmly in the soft mud.

84786.q: Which plant has very tall, woody stems and is food for pandas?
84786.e: Bamboo is a giant grass with hollow, woody stems. Giant pandas mainly eat bamboo.

84787.q: What is maple syrup made from?
a: From the sap in the trunk
84787.e: In spring people drill into the trunk of the sugar maple. The sweet sap is boiled down into syrup.
84787.m: Maple syrup comes from the tree trunk.

84788.q: What are the first leaves that grow from a seed called?
84788.e: The first leaves of a seedling are called seed leaves. They often look different from the later leaves.
84788.m: The first leaves are called seed leaves.

84789.q: Where do the big, round leaves of the water lily lie?
84789.e: The water lily is rooted in the bottom of the pond. Its leaves float flat on the water.
84789.m: Water lily leaves float on the water.

84790.q: Which bog plant catches small insects with sticky leaves?
84790.e: The sundew has leaves with sticky droplets. Insects get stuck on them and are digested.
84790.m: The sundew catches insects with its leaves.

84791.q: Where does a leaf usually have most of its tiny openings for breathing?
a: At the tip of the leaf
84791.e: Most of the stomata are on the underside of the leaf. There they are protected from the sun and lose less water.
84791.m: Leaves breathe mainly through their underside.

84792.q: Which vegetable is made of lots of tightly wrapped leaves?
84792.e: A head of cabbage is built from lots of leaves. They lie tightly on top of each other like onion skins.

84793.q: What stings your skin on the leaves of a stinging nettle?
84793.e: The stinging nettle has tiny stinging hairs. When touched, they break off and release a stinging liquid.
84793.m: The stinging nettle has stinging hairs.

84794.q: Which flowers are often used in Switzerland to make a delicious syrup?
84794.e: The white, scented flowers of the elder bloom in early summer. People soak them with sugar and lemon and make syrup from them.

84795.q: How many petals does a flower of the wild dog rose have?
84795.e: Wild roses like the dog rose have five petals. Garden roses have often been bred and have many more.
84795.m: The dog rose has five petals.

84796.q: Which shrub is also called blackthorn and has blue fruits?
84796.e: The sloe has dark twigs with sharp thorns. That is why it is also called blackthorn.
84796.m: The sloe is also called blackthorn.

84797.q: Which plant with tendrils has big orange fruits in autumn?
84797.e: The pumpkin grows long shoots with tendrils. The big fruits grow on them.

84798.q: Which scented spring flower grows from a bulb and has dense clusters of flowers?
84798.e: The hyacinth grows from a bulb. Its many flowers sit close together on one stem and smell strongly.
84798.m: The hyacinth grows from a bulb.

84799.q: What happens to a tulip bulb that you leave in the ground after flowering?
84799.e: After flowering, the tulip collects food in a new bulb. Next spring it can flower again.
84799.m: Tulips flower again every year from the bulb.

84800.e: The sweet potato forms sweet, often orange tubers. It is not closely related to the ordinary potato.
84800.m: The sweet potato is a sweet tuber.

84801.q: Which garden flower grows from tubers that are dug up in autumn?
84801.e: The dahlia forms tubers in the ground. It cannot stand frost, so the tubers are stored indoors in winter.

84802.q: What is the yellow layer you often see on cars in spring?
84802.e: In spring many trees release huge amounts of pollen. It settles as yellow dust on cars and windowsills.
84802.m: Yellow dust in spring is often pollen.

84803.q: What can you use to see single grains of pollen clearly?
84803.e: Pollen grains are tiny. Only under a microscope can you see their beautiful shapes.
84803.m: You can see pollen grains under a microscope.

84804.q: Why is there less pollen in the air after rain?
a: The rain washes it out of the air
84804.e: Raindrops carry the pollen out of the air down to the ground. That is why people with hay fever breathe more easily after rain.
84804.m: Rain washes pollen out of the air.

84805.q: What do we call plants that give bees lots of nectar and pollen?
84805.e: Plants with lots of food for bees are called bee forage. They include clover, lavender and many fruit trees.
84805.m: Bee forage plants are food plants for bees.

84806.q: What are the coloured lines on some flowers that point towards the centre for?
a: They show the way to the nectar
84806.e: These lines are called nectar guides. Like signposts, they lead insects to the nectar.
84806.m: Nectar guides show the way to the nectar.

84807.q: Which moth hovers in the air in front of flowers while it drinks nectar?
84807.e: The hummingbird hawk-moth beats its wings very fast and hovers in the air. It drinks nectar with its long proboscis.
84807.m: The hummingbird hawk-moth hovers in front of flowers.

84808.q: What colour is the cap of the fly agaric?
84808.e: The fly agaric has a bright red cap. On it are white flakes that look like spots.
84808.m: The fly agaric is red with white spots.

84809.q: Can you eat the fly agaric?
84809.e: The fly agaric is poisonous. Anyone who eats it can become seriously ill.

84810.q: What are the white spots on the fly agaric?
84810.e: The young fly agaric is wrapped in a white covering. As the cap grows, the covering tears open and pieces stay on it as flakes.
84810.m: The white spots are remains of a covering.

84811.q: Under which trees do you often find the fly agaric?
a: Under apple trees in the garden
84811.e: The fly agaric lives in a partnership with birches and spruces. That is why you often find it near them.
84811.m: The fly agaric likes to grow near birches and spruces.

84812.q: What is the fly agaric a well-known symbol of in Switzerland?
84812.e: The fly agaric is seen as a lucky charm. You often see it on New Year cards together with four-leaf clovers and chimney sweeps.
84812.m: The fly agaric is a lucky symbol.

84813.q: Where does the fly agaric probably get its name from?
a: People used to use it against flies
84813.e: In the past, people put pieces of the mushroom in milk. Flies that drank from it were stunned.
84813.m: The fly agaric used to be used against flies.

84814.q: What colour is the fly agaric under the cap and on the stem?
84814.e: Under the red cap there are lots of thin white gills. The stem is white too.
84814.m: Under the cap and on the stem, the fly agaric is white.

84815.q: In which season do you find fly agarics most often?
84815.e: Fly agarics grow from summer to autumn. You see them most often in autumn.
84815.m: You find fly agarics mainly in autumn.

84816.q: What is under the cap of a porcini mushroom?
84816.e: The porcini belongs to the boletes. Under its cap there is a sponge made of tiny tubes.
84816.m: The porcini has tubes under its cap.

84817.q: What colour is the cap of the porcini mushroom?
84817.e: The cap of the porcini is light to dark brown. It looks a little like a bread roll, which is why it is also called a penny bun.
84817.m: The porcini has a brown cap.

84818.q: What does the stem of a young porcini mushroom look like?
84818.e: Young porcini have a thick, bulging stem. It is pale with a fine net pattern.
84818.m: The porcini has a thick stem.

84819.q: Why is the porcini called “Steinpilz” (stone mushroom) in German?
a: It is as poisonous as a stone
84819.e: The flesh of the porcini is firm and solid. That is why people compared it to a stone.
84819.m: The porcini has very firm flesh.

84820.q: Is the porcini an edible mushroom?
84820.e: The porcini is thought to be one of the best edible mushrooms. You can fry it or dry it.
84820.m: The porcini is a popular edible mushroom.

84821.q: What is the porcini mushroom called in Italian?
84821.e: In Italian it is called porcino, and in the plural porcini. It is very popular in Ticino, for example in risotto.
84821.m: In Italian, the mushroom is called porcino.

84822.q: Where does the porcini mushroom grow?
84822.e: The porcini grows in forests under spruces, beeches and other trees. You find it mainly in summer and autumn.
84822.m: The porcini grows in the forest.

84823.q: How are porcini mushrooms often kept for a long time?
a: They are left in a basket in the cellar
They are put in a bowl of water
They are left in a plastic bag
84823.e: Porcini can easily be dried in slices. Dried, they keep for many months.

84824.e: The chanterelle is as bright yellow as an egg yolk. That is why it stands out in the forest.

84826.q: What does the chanterelle have under its cap?
a: Ridges that run down the stem
84826.e: The chanterelle has no real gills. It has thick, forked ridges that run down onto the stem.
84826.m: The chanterelle has ridges under its cap.

84827.q: What shape does an older chanterelle often have?
84827.e: Young chanterelles are domed. Later the middle of the cap sinks lower and the mushroom looks like a funnel.

84828.q: Which fruit does the chanterelle smell a little like?
84828.e: Many people think chanterelles have a fruity smell of apricots. This is one way to recognise them.

84829.q: Where do the chanterelles you can buy come from?
a: They are gathered in the forest
84829.e: Even today, chanterelles can hardly be grown. That is why they have to be gathered in the forest.
84829.m: Chanterelles are gathered in the forest.

84830.q: How can you recognise the false chanterelle?
a: It is orange and has thin gills
It has red spots on its cap
It has tubes instead of ridges
84830.e: The false chanterelle is orange and has thin, real gills. The true chanterelle is egg-yolk yellow and has thick ridges.
84830.m: The false chanterelle has thin gills.

84831.q: In which dish are chanterelles often eaten in Switzerland?
84831.e: Chanterelles taste good fried in a cream sauce. People often eat them with pasta, rice or bread.
84831.m: Chanterelles taste good in cream sauce.

84832.q: Which mushroom is grown most often and sold in shops?
84832.e: Button mushrooms are the best-known cultivated mushrooms. You can find them in almost every shop.
84832.m: Button mushrooms are the most common cultivated mushrooms.

84833.q: What colours are button mushrooms from the shop usually?
84833.e: In the shop there are white and brown button mushrooms. Both belong to the same species.
84833.m: Button mushrooms are white or brown.

84834.q: What are button mushrooms grown on?
a: On compost made of manure and straw
84834.e: Button mushrooms grow on soil made of manure and straw. There they find plenty of food.

84835.q: Where are button mushrooms usually grown?
84835.e: Mushrooms do not need light to grow. That is why button mushrooms are grown in dark, damp rooms.
84835.m: Button mushrooms grow in dark halls.

84836.q: What colour do the thin gills under the cap of a button mushroom turn as it gets older?
84836.e: Young button mushrooms have pink gills under the cap. As they age, the gills get darker and darker until they are chocolate brown.
84836.m: Old button mushrooms are dark brown under the cap.

84837.q: Which deadly poisonous mushroom can be mistaken for the field mushroom?
84837.e: The death cap looks similar to the field mushroom, but always has white gills. That is why mixing them up is so dangerous.
84837.m: The death cap is a dangerous lookalike.

84838.q: What does the word “champignon” mean in French?
84838.e: In French, every mushroom is called a “champignon”. In German, the word means one particular kind of mushroom.

84839.q: Where can you find field mushrooms in nature?
84839.e: The field mushroom grows on fertilised pastures and meadows. It often appears after warm rain in summer.

84840.q: What is the fine network of a fungus in the soil called?
84840.e: Under the ground, a network of fine fungal threads grows. It is called the mycelium.
84840.m: The mycelium is the fungal network in the soil.

84841.q: What is the mushroom that we see and gather in the forest?
84841.e: Most of the fungus lives out of sight as a fine network in the soil. What we see is only the fruiting body.
84841.m: We only see the fruiting body of the fungus.

84842.q: What do the threads of a fungus in the soil look like?
84842.e: Under the ground, a fungus grows as a network of very fine threads. They are as thin as hairs.
84842.m: Fungal threads in the soil are very thin.

84843.q: What does the mycelium of many forest fungi connect with?
84843.e: Many forest fungi live together with tree roots. The fungus gives the tree water and minerals, and the tree gives the fungus sugar.
84843.m: Fungi and trees help each other.

84844.q: How big can the network of a fungus in the soil become?
a: As big as many football pitches
84844.e: A honey fungus lives in the Swiss National Park. Its network in the soil is as big as many football pitches put together.
84844.m: A fungal network can become huge.

a: No, they form their own group
84845.e: Fungi are neither plants nor animals. They form their own kingdom of living things.
84845.m: Fungi are neither plants nor animals.

84846.q: What can fungi not do, unlike green plants?
84846.e: Fungi have no chlorophyll. They have to get their food from wood, leaves or living partners.
84846.m: Fungi do not make food from light.

84847.q: What important job do fungi do in the forest floor?
a: They break down leaves into soil
84847.e: Fungal threads break down dead leaves and branches. This creates new, fertile soil.
84847.m: Fungi turn leaves into new soil.

84848.q: What do fungi use to reproduce?
84848.e: Fungi produce tiny spores. A new fungal network can grow from a single spore.

84849.q: Where are the spores formed in many mushrooms with caps?
a: Right at the bottom of the stem
84849.e: The spores form on the gills or tubes under the cap. From there they fall out.
84849.m: Spores form under the mushroom cap.

84850.q: How big is a single fungal spore?
a: So small you cannot see it
84850.e: A fungal spore is tiny. You can only make it out under a microscope.

84851.q: What carries fungal spores far away?
84851.e: Spores are very light. Even a small breath of air carries them far away.

84852.q: What do you do to make a spore print?
a: You lay the mushroom cap on a piece of paper
You dip the mushroom in paint
84852.e: If you lay a mushroom cap on paper overnight, the spores fall out. They form a pattern like the gills.
84852.m: A mushroom cap on paper makes a spore print.

84853.q: What happens when you press on a ripe puffball?
a: A cloud of dust rises up
84853.e: Inside, a ripe puffball is full of spore dust. When you press on it, the spores puff out as a brown cloud.
84853.m: A ripe puffball puffs out spores.

84854.q: How many spores does a single large mushroom produce?
84854.e: A mushroom produces huge numbers of spores. Only a few of them find a good place to grow.
84854.m: A mushroom produces millions of spores.

84855.q: Which plants also reproduce with spores, like fungi?
84855.e: Ferns have no flowers and no seeds. They form spores on the underside of their fronds.

84856.q: What is the fluffy coating on old bread?
84856.e: A fungus often grows on old bread. It is called mould.
84856.m: The coating on old bread is mould.

84857.q: Which group of living things does mould belong to?
84857.e: Mould is made of fine threads like other fungi. It belongs to the fungi.

84858.q: What should you do with bread that has a spot of mould on it?
84858.e: The fungal threads grow invisibly through the whole loaf. That is why mouldy bread is thrown away completely.
84858.m: Mouldy bread is thrown away completely.

84859.q: Why should you not sniff mouldy bread?
84859.e: When you sniff it, mould spores get into your nose and lungs. That can be unhealthy.

84860.q: Where does mould especially like to grow?
a: Where it is warm and damp
Where it is freezing and dry
In the sun on the windowsill
84860.e: Moulds love warmth and moisture. In dry cold they hardly grow.
84860.m: Mould likes it warm and damp.

84861.q: What colours can mould on bread be?
84861.e: Mould on bread is often green, bluish, white or black. The colour depends on the kind of mould.

84862.q: Which cheese has a white mould that you are allowed to eat?
84862.e: Camembert is covered with a white noble mould. This mould is there on purpose and is edible.
84862.m: Camembert has an edible noble mould.

84863.q: What helps to stop bread going mouldy so quickly?
a: Wrapping it in a wet cloth
Putting it next to the cooker
Leaving it in a damp bag
84863.e: Mould needs moisture. A clean, airy bread bin keeps bread fresh for longer.
84863.m: Keeping bread dry protects it from mould.

84864.q: What does yeast do to dough?
84864.e: Yeast makes a gas in the dough. Lots of little bubbles make the dough big and airy.

84865.q: Which group of living things does baker’s yeast belong to?
84865.e: Yeast is a tiny fungus made of just one cell. A block of yeast contains billions of them.

84866.q: Which gas does yeast make in dough?
84866.e: While it works, yeast gives off carbon dioxide. The gas forms bubbles in the dough.

84867.q: What does yeast like to eat best?
84867.e: Yeast feeds on sugar. Flour also contains starch, which is turned into sugar.

84868.q: How warm should the milk be for a yeast dough?
84868.e: Yeast works best when it is pleasantly warm. In boiling liquid it dies.

84869.q: Which Swiss Sunday bread is baked with yeast?
84869.e: Zopf is a plaited yeast bread. In many families it is eaten for breakfast on Sundays.

84870.q: Where do the many holes in light, fluffy bread come from?
a: From gas bubbles made by the yeast
84870.e: During baking, the gas bubbles in the dough expand. They leave holes in the soft inside of the bread.
84870.m: Holes in bread come from gas bubbles.

84871.q: Why do you leave a yeast dough to rest before baking?
a: So that the yeast has time to work
84871.e: Yeast needs time to make gas. That is why you leave the dough covered in a warm place to rise.
84871.m: Yeast dough needs time to rise.

84872.q: What happens to the yeast in a hot oven?
84872.e: The yeast dies in the heat of the oven. But the dough stays light, because the bread sets firm.

84873.q: Where do people in Switzerland take mushrooms they have gathered if they are unsure about them?
84873.e: Many municipalities have an official mushroom inspection service. Experts there check whether the mushrooms are edible.
84873.m: Take mushrooms you are unsure about to be inspected.

84874.q: Which emergency number do you call in Switzerland in case of poisoning?
84874.e: The number 145 puts you through to Tox Info Suisse. Experts there help with poisoning around the clock.

84875.q: What is the best way to bring mushrooms to be inspected?
84875.e: The inspectors need to see all the features. That is why you bring the mushrooms whole and uncut.

84876.q: What is the best thing to carry gathered mushrooms in?
84876.e: In a basket, mushrooms stay airy and fresh. In a plastic bag they quickly go mushy and spoil.

84877.q: What do you do with a mushroom you do not know for sure?
a: You give it to the dog
84877.e: Even one poisonous mushroom can make you very ill. Never eat unknown mushrooms, not even a little bit.

84878.q: What do you call a person who officially checks gathered mushrooms?
84878.e: Mushroom inspectors have special training. They know many hundreds of kinds of mushroom.
84878.m: Mushroom inspectors know lots of mushrooms.

84879.q: Which mushroom causes the most deadly cases of mushroom poisoning?
84879.e: The death cap is extremely poisonous. Even one small mushroom can kill a person.
84879.m: The death cap is very dangerous.

84880.q: Why should you not mix unknown mushrooms with edible ones in a mushroom basket?
a: Poisonous pieces can get mixed in
84880.e: Small pieces of a poisonous mushroom can stick to other mushrooms. Then the whole collection would be dangerous.
84880.m: Poisonous mushrooms do not belong in a basket of edible ones.

84881.q: What is a lichen made of?
84881.e: A lichen is a partnership. The fungus gives protection and water, and the alga uses light to make food.
84881.m: A lichen is a fungus and an alga together.

84882.e: Lichens do not need soil. They grow on rocks, walls, roofs and tree trunks.
84882.m: Lichens grow on stones and bark.

84883.q: What do lots of lichens in a place show?
84883.e: Many lichens cannot cope with dirty air. Where they grow well, the air is usually clean.
84883.m: Many lichens are a sign of clean air.

84884.e: Many lichens grow only a few millimetres a year. That is why large lichens can be very old.

84885.q: Which animals in the far north eat lots of lichens in winter?
84885.e: Reindeer moss, which is a lichen, is an important food in winter. Reindeer scrape it out from under the snow.

84886.q: What does the map lichen look like on rocks?
84886.e: Map lichen grows yellow-green on rocks in the Alps. Black lines separate the patches like borders on a map.
84886.m: Map lichen looks like a map.

84887.q: What does beard lichen look like?
84887.e: Beard lichens form long, hanging threads. You often find them on conifers in damp mountain forests.
84887.m: Beard lichen hangs down like a beard.

84888.q: Where else can lichens live, where hardly any other plant grows?
84888.e: Lichens can survive great cold and dryness. That is why they also grow high in the mountains.
84888.m: Lichens also grow high in the mountains.

84889.e: Sometimes lots of mushrooms stand in a circle in a meadow. This circle is called a fairy ring.
84889.m: A fairy ring is a circle of mushrooms.

84890.q: Why do the mushrooms in a fairy ring grow in a circle?
a: The fungal network grows outwards from the middle
The wind blows them into a circle
Animals put them there like that
84890.e: The fungal network spreads out evenly in all directions from one point. The mushrooms form at the outer edge.
84890.m: The fungal network grows outwards in a circle.

84891.q: What did people in the past believe about fairy rings?
84891.e: In the past, people could not explain the circles of mushrooms. They said witches or elves had danced there at night.
84891.m: People used to think witches danced in mushroom circles.

84892.q: What happens to a fairy ring from year to year?
84892.e: Every year the fungal network grows a bit further outwards. That is why the circle gets bigger.
84892.m: Fairy rings get bigger every year.

84893.q: What does the grass at a fairy ring often look like?
a: Darker green than next to it
84893.e: The fungus releases nutrients that fertilise the grass. That is why the grass on the ring is often dark green.
84893.m: The grass at a fairy ring is often darker.

84894.q: How old can large fairy rings get?
84894.e: A fairy ring only grows outwards slowly. Very large rings are therefore often several hundred years old.
84894.m: Fairy rings can become very old.

84895.q: Where is a particularly good place to find fairy rings?
a: In the sand on the beach
84895.e: On an open meadow you can see the circle of mushrooms especially well. But there are fairy rings in forests too.
84895.m: Fairy rings are easy to see on meadows.

84896.q: You find a fairy ring of mushrooms. Can you just eat the mushrooms?
a: No, they must be checked first
Yes, mushrooms in a circle are always edible
84896.e: Some mushrooms are very poisonous. In Switzerland you can have gathered mushrooms checked by a mushroom inspector.
84896.m: Have mushrooms checked before you eat them.

a: In the sand on the beach
84897.e: Bracket fungi grow on living or dead trees. They feed on the wood.

84898.q: What did people use the tinder fungus for in the past?
84898.e: People made tinder from the tinder fungus. One spark was enough to make it start to glow.
84898.m: The tinder fungus helped people light fires.

84899.q: Which famous glacier mummy carried pieces of tinder fungus with him?
84899.e: Ötzi lived in the Alps over 5,000 years ago. Pieces of this bracket fungus were found among his equipment.
84899.m: Ötzi carried tinder fungus with him.

84900.q: What does the shape of many bracket fungi remind you of?
84900.e: Many bracket fungi grow sideways out of the trunk. They look like little shelves or brackets.
84900.m: Many bracket fungi look like shelves.

84901.q: What do bracket fungi do to the wood?
84901.e: Bracket fungi slowly break down the wood. This way dead wood turns back into soil.

84902.q: How can you recognise the bracket fungus called chicken of the woods from far away?
a: By its red cap with white spots
84902.e: Chicken of the woods forms large yellow to orange brackets on broadleaved trees. It is easy to see from far away.
84902.m: Chicken of the woods is bright yellow.

84903.q: What do some bracket fungi, like the tinder fungus, feel like?
84903.e: The tinder fungus is very hard and tough. It keeps growing on the same trunk for many years.
84903.m: The tinder fungus is as hard as wood.

84904.q: Which edible mushroom grows on wood and is also cultivated?
84904.e: In nature, the oyster mushroom grows on broadleaved wood. It is cultivated on straw or wood shavings.
84904.m: The oyster mushroom grows on wood.

84905.q: How should you prepare edible wild mushrooms from the forest?
84905.e: Many wild mushrooms are hard to digest or cause problems when raw. That is why you always cook them thoroughly.

84906.q: Where does the common orange lichen often grow?
84906.e: The common orange lichen forms bright yellow to orange patches. It often grows on bark, walls and roofs.
84906.m: Orange lichen grows on bark and walls.

84907.q: What is baker’s yeast called that you buy as a dry powder in a packet?
84907.e: Dried yeast has been dried and keeps for a long time. Fresh yeast, on the other hand, is a soft block from the chilled section.
84907.m: Dried yeast comes as a powder.

84908.q: Roughly how many hairs grow on a person’s head?
84908.e: A person has about 100,000 to 150,000 hairs on their head. That is so many that you cannot count them.
84908.m: About 100,000 hairs grow on the head.

84909.q: Roughly how much does a hair on your head grow in a month?
84909.e: Hair on your head grows a little bit every day. In a month that adds up to about one centimetre.
84909.m: Hair on your head grows about one centimetre a month.

84910.q: Is it normal to lose some hairs every day?
84910.e: Everyone loses about 60 to 100 hairs every day. New hairs grow back in their place.
84910.m: Every day a few hairs fall out and new ones grow back.

84911.q: Why does it not hurt when you have your hair cut?
84911.e: The visible part of the hair has no nerves. That is why you do not feel it being cut.

84912.q: What does the hair on your head protect your head from?
84912.e: Hair lies on the head like a blanket. It keeps out the sun’s rays and keeps the head warm.
84912.m: Hair protects the head from sun and cold.

84913.q: What is the place in the skin called where a hair grows from?
84913.e: Each hair sits in the scalp with its root. From there it gradually grows out.
84913.m: A hair grows from the hair root.

84914.q: What is the skin on your head, under the hair, called?
84914.e: The skin under the hair is called the scalp. The hair roots sit in it.
84914.m: Hair grows out of the scalp.

84915.q: What do you call it when a man no longer has any hair on top of his head?
84915.e: Many men lose the hair on top of their head as they get older. Then they have a bald head.
84915.m: Without hair on top of your head, you are bald.

84916.q: What do you call the line where you comb your hair to the left and right?
84916.e: The parting is the line where the hair divides. You can have it in the middle or at the side.
84916.m: The hair divides at the parting.

a: They keep sweat away from the eyes
84917.e: The eyebrows sit above the eyes like a little roof. They send sweat and raindrops off to the side.
84917.m: Eyebrows protect the eyes from sweat.

84918.q: How many eyebrows does a person normally have?
84918.e: There is one eyebrow above each eye. So a person has two eyebrows.

84919.q: What do your eyebrows often do when you are amazed?
84919.e: When you are amazed or get a fright, you raise your eyebrows. That way the face shows a feeling.
84919.m: When you are amazed, you raise your eyebrows.

84920.q: What does a face often show when the eyebrows are pulled down and together?
84920.e: When you are angry, you pull your eyebrows down and together. That way other people can see you are cross.
84920.m: We show feelings with our eyebrows.

84921.e: Eyebrows are lots of short hairs above the eyes. They grow much less long than the hair on your head.

a: Similar to the hair on your head
84922.e: Eyebrows are usually a similar colour to the hair on your head. With fair hair they are often fair too.
84922.m: Eyebrows are usually a similar colour to the hair on your head.

84923.q: Which tool do you use to pluck out single eyebrow hairs?
84923.e: Tweezers have two fine tips. You can use them to grip a single hair and pull it out.
84923.m: You grip single hairs with tweezers.

84924.q: What are the short hairs on the edge of the eyelids called?
84924.e: Eyelashes grow on the edge of the eyelids. They stand in front of the eye like a little fence.

84925.q: What do eyelashes protect the eye from?
84925.e: Eyelashes keep dust and small particles away from the eye. If something touches the eyelashes, the eye closes quickly.
84925.m: Eyelashes protect the eye from dust.

84926.q: What does your eye do when something touches your eyelashes?
84926.e: Eyelashes are very sensitive. When they are touched, you blink straight away, which protects the eye.
84926.m: When our eyelashes are touched, we blink.

84927.q: On which eyelids do eyelashes grow?
84927.e: Eyelashes grow on the upper and the lower eyelid. At the top they are usually longer and more numerous.
84927.m: Eyelashes grow on the upper and lower lid.

84928.q: Where are the eyelashes usually longer?
84928.e: On the upper eyelid, the eyelashes are longer and there are more of them. At the bottom they are shorter.
84928.m: The eyelashes are longer at the top than at the bottom.

84929.q: What happens when an eyelash falls out?
84929.e: Eyelashes fall out from time to time, just like other hairs. Afterwards a new eyelash grows back.
84929.m: An eyelash that falls out grows back.

84930.q: Which large animal is known for its especially long eyelashes?
84930.e: Camels have long, thick eyelashes. They protect their eyes from sand in the desert.
84930.m: Camels have long eyelashes against the sand.

84931.q: What is the quick closing and opening of the eyelids called?
84931.e: When you blink, the lids close briefly and open again. The eyelashes sweep along and the eye is kept moist.
84931.m: When you blink, your eyelids close briefly.

84932.q: What do you call hair that twists like a spiral?
84932.e: Hair that twists or frizzes is called curls. Other hair hangs down straight.

84933.q: What do you call hair that hangs straight down?
84933.e: Straight hair has no waves and no curls. It falls straight down.
84933.m: Hair that hangs straight is called straight hair.

84934.q: What decides whether a hair grows straight or curly?
84934.e: Whether a hair grows straight or curly depends on its shape and the shape of the hair root. Straight hairs are rounder in cross-section, curly ones flatter or oval.
84934.m: Curly hairs are flatter than straight hairs.

84935.q: Which device can you use to give straight hair curls for a while?
84935.e: A curling iron is hot. You wrap a strand of hair around it, and the hair stays curly for a while.
84935.m: You make curls with a curling iron.

84936.q: What are the little rolls called that you wrap wet hair around to make curls?
84936.e: You wrap wet hair around curlers and let it dry. Afterwards the hair is curly.
84936.m: Curlers turn straight hair into curls.

84937.q: What do you call hair that is slightly wavy but not very curly?
84937.e: Wavy hair is between straight and curly. It has soft waves.

84938.q: Do children with curly-haired parents often get curls too?
a: No, only straight hair is inherited
84938.e: Whether someone has curls is often inherited from their parents. That is why brothers and sisters often have similar hair.
84938.m: Curls are often inherited from your parents.

84939.q: Which animal often has a thick, curly coat that is made into wool?
84939.e: Sheep have a thick, crinkly coat. It is sheared and made into wool.

84940.q: What hair colour do many people get when they grow old?
84940.e: In old age, hair makes less and less pigment. That is why hair goes grey and later white.
84940.m: In old age, hair goes grey.

84941.e: There is a natural pigment in hair. A lot of dark pigment makes dark hair; a little makes fair hair.
84941.m: A pigment in the hair decides the hair colour.

84942.q: What do you call light yellow hair?
84942.e: Light yellow hair is called blond. Many small children have blond hair that gets darker later.

84943.q: Which hair colour is most common in the whole world?
84943.e: Most people in the world have black or dark brown hair. Blond and other light hair is much rarer.

84944.q: Which natural hair colour is very rare?
84944.e: Only a few people have naturally red hair. Red is the rarest natural hair colour.

84945.q: What can make fair hair even fairer in summer?
84945.e: Sunlight bleaches the pigment in hair. That is why fair hair often gets even fairer in summer.

84946.q: What can you use to change your hair colour artificially?
84946.e: With hair dye you can colour hair a different colour. Newly growing hair has its own colour again.
84946.m: You can colour hair with hair dye.

84947.q: What is dark brown hair often called?
84947.e: Dark brown hair is also called brunette. The word comes from French.
84947.m: Dark brown hair is called brunette.

84948.q: What do you call the hair that falls straight over the forehead?
84948.e: A fringe is short-cut hair over the forehead. It hangs in front of the forehead like a curtain.
84948.m: The hair over the forehead is called a fringe.

84949.q: What is the hairstyle called where three strands of hair are woven together?
84949.e: For a plait, you weave three strands over each other in turn. That way long hair stays tidy.
84949.m: A plait is woven from three strands.

84950.q: What is the hairstyle called where long hair is twisted into a knot on the head?
84950.e: For a bun, you twist the long hair together and pin it as a knot. That way it does not get in the way, for example during sport.
84950.m: A bun is a knot of hair.

84951.q: What is the hairstyle called where the hair is tied together at the back with a band and hangs down?
84951.e: For a ponytail, you tie the hair together at the back of the head. It then hangs down like a horse’s tail.
84951.m: A ponytail is tied with a hair tie.

84952.q: Why do you have to have your hair cut again and again?
84952.e: The hair on your head keeps growing all year. So that it does not get too long, you cut it now and then.
84952.m: Hair keeps growing, so you cut it.

84953.q: What do you call a hairstyle where the hair is short and sticks up like bristles?
84953.e: With a crew cut, the hair is very short and sticks up. It looks a little like a hedgehog’s spines.
84953.m: With a crew cut, short hair sticks up.

84954.q: What do you use to hold a ponytail together?
84954.e: A hair tie is a stretchy band. You wrap it around the hair so it stays together.
84954.m: A hair tie holds the hair together.

84955.q: What do you use to dry wet hair with warm air?
84955.e: A hairdryer blows warm air. It makes wet hair dry faster.
84955.m: You dry your hair with a hairdryer.

84956.q: What is the job called where you cut other people’s hair?
84956.e: A hairdresser cuts other people’s hair. In Switzerland, people usually call a hairdresser a ‘Coiffeur’.

84957.q: What does the hairdresser often do first, before cutting your hair?
84957.e: Usually the hair is washed first. Wet hair is easy to comb and cut straight.
84957.m: At the hairdresser’s, your hair is often washed first.

84958.q: What does the hairdresser cut hair with?
84958.e: Hairdressing scissors are especially sharp. With them the hairdresser can cut hair precisely.
84958.m: The hairdresser cuts with hairdressing scissors.

84959.q: What does the hairdresser put around you so that no hair falls on your clothes?
84959.e: The cape covers your clothes. The cut-off hair falls onto it and not onto your T-shirt.
84959.m: A cape protects your clothes during a haircut.

84960.q: Which device does a hairdresser use to cut hair very short, almost like stubble?
84960.e: Hair clippers cut lots of hair short at once. They are used for very short hairstyles.
84960.m: Hair clippers make hair very short.

84961.q: What is the hairdresser called who especially looks after men’s beards?
84961.e: A barber cuts hair and shaves or trims beards. In the past, many villages had a barber.

84963.q: What is the shop called where the hairdresser works?
84963.e: The hairdresser works in a hair salon. There are mirrors, chairs and basins for washing hair there.
84963.m: The hairdresser works in a hair salon.

84964.q: What do you use a hairbrush for?
84964.e: You use a hairbrush to untangle your hair. Afterwards it lies smooth and tidy.
84964.m: You tidy your hair with a hairbrush.

84965.q: What does a comb have instead of bristles?
84965.e: A comb has a row of teeth. With it you can tidy your hair and make a parting.

84966.q: What is the best way to brush long, tangled hair?
a: With lots of force from the top
84966.e: You start at the bottom with the ends and slowly work your way up. That way the hair breaks less and it hurts less.
84966.m: Brush long hair from the bottom up.

84967.q: Why should you clean your hairbrush now and then?
a: Because hair and dirt collect in it
84967.e: Hair that has fallen out, dust and grease get caught in the brush. A clean brush looks after your hair better.
84967.m: You should clean a hairbrush regularly.

84968.q: What are the many little sticks on a hairbrush called?
84968.e: A hairbrush has lots of bristles. They can be made of plastic or animal hair.

84969.q: What forms in long hair if you do not brush it for a long time?
84969.e: Unbrushed long hair gets tangled. This forms knots that are hard work to untangle.
84969.m: Without brushing, long hair gets knots.

84970.q: What do you use to groom the coat of a dog or horse?
84970.e: Animals with fur are brushed too. This removes loose hairs and dirt.

84971.e: The head louse is a tiny insect without wings. It lives in the hair on people’s heads.
84971.m: The head louse is a small insect.

84972.q: What does a head louse feed on?
84972.e: The head louse bites into the scalp and sucks a little blood. It does this several times a day.

84973.q: How do head lice usually get from one head to another?
a: They crawl across when heads touch
84973.e: Head lice can neither fly nor jump. They crawl across when heads touch, for example when playing.
84973.m: Lice crawl from head to head.

84974.q: What are the eggs of head lice called?
84974.e: The eggs of lice are called nits. They stick firmly to the hairs close to the scalp.
84974.m: The eggs of lice are called nits.

84975.q: Which sign can point to head lice?
84975.e: Lice bites itch. If you often scratch your head, you should have it checked.

84976.q: What do you use to comb lice out of hair?
84976.e: A nit comb has teeth that are very close together. Lice and nits get caught in the comb.
84976.m: You comb out lice with a nit comb.

84977.q: Do you get head lice because you are dirty?
a: No, it can happen to anyone
84977.e: Head lice are found in clean hair too. They spread through head contact, not through dirt.
84977.m: Head lice have nothing to do with dirt.

84978.q: Where does a louse prefer to lay its eggs?
a: At the ends of the hair
84978.e: The louse glues its eggs to the hairs close to the scalp. It is warm there, and the young hatch after about a week.
84978.m: Nits stick close to the scalp.

84979.q: Roughly how big is an adult head louse?
84979.e: An adult head louse is about 3 millimetres long. That is about the size of a sesame seed.
84979.m: A head louse is only about 3 millimetres big.

a: Small flakes of skin from the scalp
84980.e: Dandruff is skin cells that have come loose. The flakes are usually small and come off the scalp.
84980.m: Dandruff is small flakes of scalp.

84981.e: Dandruff is usually small white or slightly yellowish flakes. They look a bit like crumbs.

84982.q: Where can you see dandruff especially well?
84982.e: White dandruff stands out especially on dark jumpers or jackets. On light fabrics you can hardly see it.
84982.m: You can see dandruff well on dark clothes.

84983.q: What can you often treat dandruff with?
84983.e: There are special shampoos for dandruff. They calm the scalp.
84983.m: A special shampoo often helps with dandruff.

84984.e: Dandruff comes from your own scalp. You cannot pass it on to others like an illness.

84985.q: What does the skin do all the time, even without you noticing?
84985.e: New cells are always forming deep in the skin. At the top, old cells come off as tiny flakes.
84985.m: The skin renews itself all the time.

84986.q: How can you tell dandruff apart from nits?
a: Dandruff can easily be shaken off
84986.e: Dandruff lies loosely on the hair and falls off easily. Nits, on the other hand, stick firmly to the hair.
84986.m: Dandruff can be shaken off, nits cannot.

84987.q: How many toenails does a person normally have?
84987.e: Each foot has five toes with one nail each. Together that makes ten toenails.

84988.q: Which toenail is usually the biggest?
a: The nail of the big toe
The nail of the little toe
They are all the same size
The nail of the middle toe
84988.e: The big toe is the thickest toe. That is why it also has the biggest nail.
84988.m: The big toe has the biggest nail.

84989.q: What can happen if a toenail is cut too short and round?
84989.e: A nail cut too round can grow into the skin at the side. This hurts and can become inflamed.
84989.m: Toenails should not be cut too short.

84990.q: When are toenails easier to cut?
84990.e: Warm water makes the nails a little softer. Then they are easier to cut.
84990.m: After a bath, nails are softer.

84991.q: What colour does a toenail often turn if you stub your toe hard?
84991.e: After a knock, blood can collect under the nail. Then the nail looks dark blue or black.
84991.m: A bruise turns the nail dark.

a: They protect the tips of the toes
84992.e: Toenails are hard like a little plate. They protect the sensitive tips of the toes from above.

84993.q: Why should shoes have enough room for your toes at the front?
a: So the toenails are not squashed
84993.e: If shoes are too tight at the front, they press on the toenails. This hurts and can injure the nails.
84993.m: Good shoes give your toes room.

84994.q: What happens to a toenail that comes off because of an injury?
a: Usually a new one grows back
84994.e: If the nail root stays healthy, a new nail grows back. But it takes many months.
84994.m: A lost toenail usually grows back slowly.

84995.q: What shape are the blades of nail scissors often?
84995.e: Many nail scissors have slightly curved blades. That way you can cut your fingernails nicely round.
84995.m: Nail scissors often have curved blades.

84996.q: Which other tool can you use instead of nail scissors to shorten your nails?
84996.e: Nail clippers press two sharp edges together and cut off the nail. Many people use them instead of scissors.
84996.m: You can also shorten nails with nail clippers.

84997.q: What can you use to smooth rough nail edges after cutting?
84997.e: After cutting, the edges can be rough. You rub them smooth with a nail file.
84997.m: You smooth your nails with a nail file.

84998.q: Why should small children only use nail scissors with help?
a: Because they are pointed and sharp
84998.e: Nail scissors are pointed and sharp. You can easily cut your finger with them.
84998.m: You have to be careful with nail scissors.

84999.q: Why is it best for each person in the family to have their own nail scissors?
a: So no germs are passed on
84999.e: Fungi or germs can stick to nail scissors. With your own scissors you do not pass them on.
84999.m: Your own nail scissors are more hygienic.

85000.q: What is the best way to cut your fingernails?
a: Slightly round, following the shape of the finger
Right down to the nail bed
85000.e: You cut fingernails slightly round, the same shape as the fingertip. Toenails, on the other hand, are cut more straight.

85001.q: Where do you keep nail scissors safely?
85001.e: In a case, the pointed scissors are protected. That way you do not prick yourself and the scissors stay clean.
85001.m: Nail scissors belong in a case.

85002.e: The eyebrows grow on a small arch of bone above the eyes. The eyelids are underneath.
85002.m: The eyebrows are above the eyes.

85003.q: Which brush do people often use together with a hairdryer to style their hair?
85003.e: A round brush is round like a roller. You turn the hair around it and blow-dry it, which gives it bounce.
85003.m: You style hair with a round brush and a hairdryer.

85004.q: Does scratching your head hard help against dandruff?
a: Yes, but only with a comb
85004.e: Scratching irritates the scalp even more. Then it can itch and flake even more.
85004.m: Scratching does not make dandruff better.

85005.q: Roughly how often do you need to cut your fingernails?
a: About every one to two weeks
85005.e: Fingernails grow slowly but steadily. That is why you cut them about every one to two weeks.
85005.m: Cut your fingernails about every one to two weeks.

85006.q: What grows more slowly: hair on your head or grass in summer?
85006.e: In summer, grass can grow several centimetres in a week. In that time, a hair on your head grows only a few millimetres.
85006.m: Hair grows more slowly than grass in summer.

85007.q: What is the black colour called that some adults use to make their eyelashes darker?
85007.e: Mascara is a colour for the eyelashes. It makes the eyelashes look darker and longer.

85008.q: What does a cork do when you throw it into water?
85008.e: Cork is very light and full of tiny air bubbles. That is why a cork floats on the water.
85008.m: A cork floats on the water.

85009.q: Why does an empty, closed plastic bottle float?
a: Because it is full of air
85009.e: There is air in the bottle, and air is much lighter than water. That is why the bottle stays on top.
85009.m: Things that contain a lot of air often float.

85010.q: What happens to a plastic bottle when you fill it completely with sand?
85010.e: Filled with sand, the bottle is much heavier than the same amount of water. That is why it goes under.
85010.m: A bottle filled with sand sinks.

85011.q: What floats on the water in a puddle after rain?
85011.e: A dry leaf is very light and flat. It stays lying on top of the water.
85011.m: A leaf floats on the water.

85012.q: Which animal can float on the water without paddling?
85012.e: Ducks have thick, oily feathers with lots of air between them. This lets them float easily on the water.
85012.m: Ducks float easily on the water.

85013.q: What happens if you breathe in deeply in the water and lie still?
85013.e: With air in your lungs, your body is lighter for its size. That is why you float better.
85013.m: Air in your lungs helps you float in water.

85014.q: You put a piece of wood and a stone in water. What happens?
a: The wood floats, the stone sinks
The stone floats, the wood sinks
85014.e: Wood is lighter than the same amount of water and stays on top. A stone is heavier and goes under.
85014.m: You can test what floats and what sinks.

85015.q: What happens to a metal spoon in water?
85015.e: A metal spoon is heavier than the same amount of water. That is why it goes under.
85015.m: A metal spoon sinks in water.

85016.q: What does a glass do when it fills up completely with water?
85016.e: An empty glass can float as long as there is air in it. If it fills with water, it goes under.

85017.q: What do you call the bottom of a lake, where sunken things lie?
85017.e: Things that sink in a lake end up on the lake bed. Stones, mud and sometimes lost things lie there.
85017.m: Sunken things lie on the lake bed.

85018.q: What happens to a ball of modelling clay in water?
85018.e: A solid ball of clay is heavier than the same amount of water. That is why it goes under.
85018.m: A ball of modelling clay sinks.

85019.q: How can you shape modelling clay so that it floats on water?
85019.e: Shaped like a boat, the clay pushes aside a lot of water and has air inside. Then it can float.
85019.m: Shaped like a boat, even clay can float.

85020.q: What happens to a ship when a lot of water flows in through a hole?
85020.e: The water coming in makes the ship heavier and heavier. When there is too much water inside, it goes under.
85020.m: A ship with a leak can sink.

85021.q: What is the heavy metal part called that a ship drops to the bottom so it does not drift away?
85021.e: The anchor is heavy and sinks to the bottom. There it holds the ship in place.
85021.m: The anchor keeps the ship in its place.

85022.q: Which usually sinks in a bowl of water: an apple or a potato?
85022.e: An apple has lots of air between its cells, so it floats. A potato is denser and usually goes under.

85023.q: What is the force called with which water pushes things upwards?
85023.e: Water pushes from below against everything in it. This upward force is called buoyancy.
85023.m: Buoyancy pushes things in water upwards.

85024.q: Why do you feel lighter in the swimming pool than on land?
85024.e: Buoyancy acts in water. It carries part of your weight, so you feel lighter.

85025.q: What happens to the water in the bath when you get in?
85025.e: Your body takes up space in the water and pushes the water aside. That is why the water level rises.
85025.m: When you get into the bath, the water rises.

85026.q: Which Greek scientist is said to have shouted “Eureka” in the bath?
85026.e: Archimedes lived more than 2,000 years ago. According to a story, he discovered in the bath how objects push water aside.

85027.q: Why does a huge steel ship float?
a: Because it is hollow and full of air
Because steel is lighter than water
85027.e: A steel ship is hollow inside. With all the air in the hull, it is lighter than the same amount of water, so it floats.
85027.m: A steel ship floats because it is hollow inside.

85028.q: What is easier to lift in water than on land?
85028.e: In water, buoyancy helps to carry things. That is why you can lift a heavy stone more easily under water.
85028.m: Heavy things are easier to lift in water.

85029.q: Which way does buoyancy point in water?
85029.e: Buoyancy always works against gravity. Gravity pulls down, buoyancy pushes up.

85030.q: Which way do air bubbles move in water?
85030.e: Air is much lighter than water. That is why air bubbles rise in water.

85031.q: Why does a rowing boat tip easily when everyone sits on the same side?
85031.e: If everyone sits on one side, a lot of weight pushes the boat down there. So in a boat you spread the weight evenly.
85031.m: In a boat, you spread the weight evenly.

85032.q: What is a simple craft made of tree trunks tied together called?
85032.e: A raft is made of logs tied together. Because wood floats, the raft carries people and things.
85032.m: A raft is made of logs tied together.

85033.q: What happens to a boat when you load it heavier and heavier?
a: It sits lower in the water
85033.e: The more load in the boat, the deeper it sinks into the water. If it is too heavy, water gets in.
85033.m: A heavily loaded boat sits low in the water.

85034.q: What is a narrow boat called that you move with a single-bladed paddle?
85034.e: In a canoe you sit or kneel and paddle with a paddle. Canoes are light and narrow.
85034.m: You move a canoe with a paddle.

85035.q: Which old ships with big paddle wheels still sail on Lake Lucerne today?
85035.e: Old paddle steamers still sail on some Swiss lakes. A steam engine turns their big paddle wheels.
85035.m: Steamships still sail on Swiss lakes.

85036.q: What is the part of a boat that points forwards called?
